anomalies.observed: Net TX_GPIO14 contains the CM4 UART TX line (Module1 pin 55 GPIO14) and FT231XS RXD (U21 pin 4), but it also contains the 3.3 V LDO output U20 pin 2 (VO), U21 pin 15 (VCC), and many 3.3 V decoupling capacitors.
anomalies.expected: The 3.3 V rail should be a separate power net (e.g. +3V3) from the UART TX_GPIO14 signal; Module1 pin 55 and U21 pin 4 should not be tied to the 3.3 V supply.
anomalies.impact: The 3.3 V supply is shorted to the CM4 GPIO14 UART TX and FT231XS RXD input. This breaks serial communication and can cause contention or excessive current if GPIO14 is driven low.

anomalies.observed: R60 connects D30 pin 2 (K2) to ESTOP_OUT, while D30 pin 4 (A2) is also on ESTOP_OUT. The resistor is therefore connected directly across the second LED of D30.
anomalies.expected: R60 should be a series current-limiting resistor between D30 K2 and GND (or another return) so the LED can be forward-biased, not a connection back to A2/ESTOP_OUT.
anomalies.impact: The second D30 LED is bypassed by R60 and will not illuminate, so any ESTOP_OUT indicator function is lost.

anomalies.observed: Net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23; no supply pin, buffer output, connector, or other source is on this net.
anomalies.expected: These LED anodes need a 3.3 V or switched LED power source so current can flow through the LEDs.
anomalies.impact: D4, D14, and D23 are unpowered and will never illuminate, removing those indicator functions.

parsed.summary: The design contains multiple clear anomalies, most critically a merged 3.3 V power rail with the TX_GPIO14 UART net, plus a shorted D30 indicator LED and a floating LED anode net.
